questions.enonce_markdown: For each substance identify the chemical bond holding the particles and describe how the bond is formed. *[17 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Magnesium chloride, $\mathrm{MgCl_2}$: ionic (electrovalent) bond.**

A magnesium atom (2, 8, 2) **loses its 2 outer electrons** to become $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ (2, 8). Each chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) **gains 1 electron** to become $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ (2, 8, 8). Two chlorine atoms are needed for the two electrons: $\mathrm{Mg} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg^{2+}} + 2e^-$ and $\mathrm{Cl_2} + 2e^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cl^-}$. The oppositely charged ions attract each other strongly (electrostatic attraction) and form a giant ionic lattice.

**Copper, Cu: metallic bond.**

Each copper atom gives up its outer (valence) electron(s), which become **delocalised**; the lattice of positive copper ions is held together by the **electrostatic attraction between the positive ions and the 'sea' of mobile electrons**.

**Methane, $\mathrm{CH_4}$: covalent bond.**

Carbon (2, 4) needs 4 more electrons and each hydrogen (1) needs 1. The carbon atom **shares one pair of electrons with each of four hydrogen atoms**, forming four single covalent bonds; each hydrogen then has 2 electrons and carbon has 8 in its outer shell. The molecule is tetrahedral and the molecules are held to each other only by weak intermolecular forces.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one physical property of each substance. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **Magnesium chloride:** high melting point (a hard, brittle crystalline solid); it **conducts electricity when molten or dissolved in water**, but not as a solid; it is soluble in water.
- **Copper:** a good conductor of electricity and heat; malleable and ductile; shiny; high melting point.
- **Methane:** a gas at room temperature with a very low melting and boiling point; it does not conduct electricity; it is insoluble in water.

(One property for each substance is enough.)
